explanation: Transpose the square matrix across its main diagonal, then reverse every row. Together these operations rotate values clockwise while preserving the original matrix and row objects.
timeComplexity: O(n squared) time for an n by n matrix.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Transposition maps each original cell (r,c) to (c,r), and reversing each row then maps it to (c,n-1-r). That is exactly the clockwise quarter-turn coordinate transformation. Only values are swapped, so the original matrix and row objects remain the same.
walkthrough: For [[2,5],[7,9]], transposition produces [[2,7],[5,9]]. Reversing both rows yields [[7,2],[9,5]], the clockwise rotation. The judge checks the changed original matrix rather than a replacement object.
edgeCases: The input matrix must be square.
The original row objects must be preserved.
